headline: Record quarter; by-product credits push cash cost negative

kpis.label: C1 cash cost (Cu, net of by-product credits)

summary_short: Record revenue of $757.3M and adjusted EBITDA of $421.9M, with consolidated C1 cash cost swinging to $(1.80)/lb copper on strong gold by-product credits. Ended the quarter with over $1 billion of cash and reaffirmed full-year 2026 production and cost guidance.
summary_long: Revenue of $757.3M rose 3.3% q/q and 27.3% y/y, with adjusted EBITDA of $421.9M up 9.3% q/q on higher copper realizations and steady gold volumes. Net income was $190.4M ($0.48/share basic and diluted), operating cash flow $211.3M and free cash flow $102.3M. Consolidated C1 cash cost fell to $(1.80)/lb copper net of by-product credits, well below the $(0.30) to $(0.10) 2026 guidance range; AISC was $0.73/lb against a $1.70 to $2.10 range. Production was 27,929t copper and 61,700oz gold, on track for full-year targets that were reaffirmed. The balance sheet ended with $1,003.8M cash and $1,009.4M long-term debt — roughly neutral. New Ingerbelle permits received.
confidence_notes: Shard eventDate 2026-04-15 was an estimator placeholder; replaced with actual release date 2026-05-01 from the primary. C1 and AISC are consolidated and net of by-product credits (gold, silver, zinc, molybdenum); Hudbay does not publish gross-of-credits cash cost. Negative C1 reflects by-product revenue exceeding cash operating cost — normal for a polymetallic copper miner with strong gold co-product economics, not an accounting anomaly.
